To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel approach to analyze delay tolerant networks, based on a combination of a novel branching process with migration and the theory of branching random walks, and that our approach is applicable to a broad class of mobility models.
We have developed a new analytical framework for studying delay-tolerant networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a mathematical model for the dynamics of the propagation of information in delay-tolerant networks.
the analysis of the dynamics of the spread of information in a delay tolerant networks (also known as disruption tolerant networks).
a mathematical model for a class of DTNs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the branching process with migration model in the context of DTNs is an excellent tool that can provide useful insight into the performance of the network, and is also very practical, since the parameters that appear in the expressions for the performance measures can be estimated from the data.
the use of branching processes with migration is a powerful tool to model the propagation of packets through a DTN.
the use of branching processes with migration in the study of the performance of DTNs is a promising approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to apply branching processes to delay tolerant networks.
we are able to provide analytical results for the number of copies in the system for a wide range of mobility models and for a wide range (in terms of parameters) of the DTN.
we have developed an approach for analyzing DTNs using a combination of stochastic process and queuing theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it allows to derive analytical expressions for performance metrics of DTNs, and that it can be used to compare different mobility models in DTNs.
a simple branching process can capture a lot of the complexity of DTNs.
a simple mobility model can be sufficient to obtain accurate performance results for the dynamics of a DTN.
